title: CBI Nears Chargesheet in Twisha Sharma Dowry Death Case Against Ex-Judge and Son
excerpt: A Bhopal court directed the CBI to file its final report by August 11 against retired judge Giribala Singh and her son Samarth Singh, accused in the alleged dowry death of model-turned-actress Twisha Sharma.
body:
• The CBI was directed by a Bhopal court to file its chargesheet by August 11 in the alleged dowry death of model-turned-actress Twisha Sharma
  • Retired judge Giribala Singh and her son Samarth Singh remain in judicial custody on charges of dowry-related harassment, mental abuse, and domestic violence
  • An AIIMS forensic report found skin tissue on the gymnastics belt allegedly used as a ligature, resolving a key dispute in the case
  • The court earlier rejected Giribala Singh's bail plea, calling the charges against her "serious"

CBI Probe Reaches Final Stage

The Central Bureau of Investigation's probe into the death of model-turned-actress Twisha Sharma has entered its final phase, with a Bhopal court directing the agency to submit its chargesheet by August 11 against retired judge Giribala Singh and her son Samarth Singh.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2089267224641163733

Sharma, a 25-year-old Noida resident, was found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal's Katara Hills area on May 12, 2026 — just five months after her marriage to Samarth Singh, a Bhopal-based lawyer, on December 9, 2025. Her family alleges she was driven to death by sustained dowry harassment, mental abuse, and domestic violence at the hands of her husband and mother-in-law.

Key Forensic Findings

The case took a critical forensic turn when the AIIMS medical board, which conducted a court-ordered second postmortem, submitted its sealed findings to the CBI in July. A major point of contention was whether a gymnastics belt with a metal ring, found at the scene, was the actual ligature used. The AIIMS report confirmed the presence of skin tissue on the belt, according to reports — a finding that could prove pivotal in establishing the circumstances of Sharma's death.

The initial postmortem had confirmed "antemortem hanging" as the cause of death but noted six to seven additional injuries on Sharma's body, including marks on her left arm, finger, and head. A subsequent inquiry confirmed these injuries were not caused during removal of the body or transportation to the hospital, according to the Madhya Pradesh High Court order.

The Investigation So Far

The Supreme Court directed the CBI to take over the investigation in late May, after multiple legal challenges were filed across the trial court, High Court, and apex court. The CBI registered the case on May 25 under Sections 80(2), 85, and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, according to Latestly.

The FIR includes a specific allegation that Giribala Singh demanded ₹2 lakh from Sharma's family during the vidai ceremony in December 2025, NDTV reported. Sharma's family further alleges that she was pressured to terminate a pregnancy and was subjected to continuous mental harassment.

"From the WhatsApp chats also, it cannot be said that the allegations are only against Samarth Singh."

— Madhya Pradesh High Court, while cancelling Giribala Singh's anticipatory bail

The High Court cancelled Giribala Singh's anticipatory bail on May 28 in a 17-page order, observing that the trial court had failed to examine crucial material facts. Both accused were arrested and have remained in judicial custody since, with their latest extension running through August 11.

Bail Denied, Custody Extended

On July 25, Special Judge Ram Pratap Mishra rejected Giribala Singh's bail application, observing that the charges against her were "serious." The defence had argued on humanitarian grounds, citing Singh's age, health issues, a nearly 100-year-old mother who depended on her care, and a burglary at her residence while she was in custody, according to the Times of India.

The Singh family has denied all allegations, claiming Sharma suffered from substance abuse and emotional instability — claims her family has firmly rejected.

What's Next

The CBI's chargesheet, expected to be filed at the August 11 hearing, marks a decisive stage in a case that has gripped national attention. The charges, the forensic evidence from AIIMS, and the WhatsApp records cited by the High Court will form the foundation of the prosecution's case as it moves toward trial. Both accused remain in judicial custody as the court awaits the agency's final report.
nri_angle: The case has drawn attention from NRIs concerned about dowry-related violence and judicial accountability in India, particularly given the accused's judicial background.
